description: The number twenty-four is associated with worship and organized priestly service. David arranged the priests into twenty-four divisions for temple service. In Revelation, twenty-four elders sit around God's throne and worship. Thus, this number links the Old Testament arrangement of priestly service with heavenly worship in the New Testament.

footnotes.text: David organized the priests into 24 divisions (mishmarot) for service in the temple (1 Chr 24:1–19). This arrangement continued throughout the temple period and is mentioned in the Mishnah (Ta'anit 4:2).
The twenty-four elders in Revelation (Rev 4:4, 10–11) are often seen as representatives of all God's people—twelve for the tribes of Israel and twelve for the apostles—united in eternal worship.

In the Jewish temple service, the twenty-four priestly divisions rotated so that each division served about two weeks a year. Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist, belonged to Abijah's division—the eighth of the twenty-four (Luke 1:5).
